title: What to put in an owner statement (with an example layout)
summary: What to include in a vacation rental owner statement: summary, reservations, expenses, management fee and payout, with an example layout.
body_markdown:
[All posts](https://prohost.ai/blog)


**An owner statement answers one question: how much money is the owner getting this month, and why? A good one fits on a page and has six parts: the header, a summary, every reservation, every expense, your management fee, and the payout. Below is what goes in each part, an example layout you can copy, and the mistakes that cause most owner questions.**


## Key takeaways


- **Lead with the number.** The net payout to the owner goes at the top, with the three or four numbers that produce it.
- **Show every reservation and every expense** with a date, a listing and an amount. Owners trust what they can trace.
- **Say exactly how the fee is calculated:** the percentage, and what it's a percentage of (gross rent, or rent after cleaning fees and channel fees).
- **Attach receipts** for any expense over a threshold you agree with the owner in writing.
- **Send it on the same day every month,** and pay on the same day too.

## Where we're coming from


I spent 6 years at Airbnb as a staff data scientist on the hosting team, and we host in Hawaii, the Smokies and Joshua Tree. Property managers on ProhostAI tell us the same thing: owners rarely question the payout itself. They question the line they can't explain. Every section below exists to remove one of those questions.


## What to put in an owner statement


### 1. Header


- Your company name, address, phone and email.
- The owner's name and address.
- The property (or properties) covered.
- The statement period, for example "October 1 to October 31, 2026".
- A statement number and the date it was issued.


### 2. Summary


Four to six lines that add up to the payout:


- Gross rental revenue
- Less: channel and payment fees (if they're deducted before you receive the money)
- Less: management fee
- Less: expenses
- Plus or less: adjustments (refunds, damage claims, last month's corrections)
- **Net payout to owner**


### 3. Reservations


One row per stay in the period: guest name or reservation code, channel, check-in and check-out dates, nights, rent, cleaning fee, other fees, channel fee, and net. Say which rule you use for stays that cross month end (by check-in date, by check-out date, or by night). Pick one and stick to it.


### 4. Expenses


One row per expense: date, vendor, category (cleaning, maintenance, supplies, utilities), a short description and the amount. Mark which expenses are passed through at cost and which carry a markup, if your agreement allows one.


### 5. Management fee


The rate, the base it's calculated on, and the result. For example: "20% of rent after channel fees, excluding cleaning fees: 20% × $6,180 = $1,236."


### 6. Payout


The amount, the date it was sent or will be sent, and the method (bank transfer, check). If you hold a reserve for repairs, show the opening balance, what was added or used, and the closing balance.


### 7. Notes (optional, short)


Two or three lines: occupancy for the month, anything that happened (a repair, a review worth noting), and anything coming up (a booked deep clean, a planned replacement).


## Example layout (copy this)


All amounts below are made up for illustration.


Owner statement · October 1 to October 31, 2026 · Statement #1042


Owner \[Owner name\], \[address\]


Property \[Property name\]


Gross rental revenue (rent plus cleaning fees) $7,220.00


Less channel fees −$566.10


Less management fee (20% of rent after channel fees, excl. cleaning fees) −$1,210.78


Less expenses −$1,312.40


**Net payout to owner** (sent by ACH on November 5) **$4,130.72**


Reservation Channel Dates Nights Rent Cleaning fee Channel fee Net


HM1234 Airbnb Oct 2 to Oct 6 4 $1,480.00 $200.00 −$260.40 $1,419.60


VR5678 Vrbo Oct 10 to Oct 17 7 $2,590.00 $200.00 −$223.20 $2,566.80


D-9012 Direct Oct 22 to Oct 27 5 $2,550.00 $200.00 −$82.50 $2,667.50


Total $6,620.00 $600.00 −$566.10 $6,653.90


Date Vendor Category Description Amount


Oct 6 \[Cleaner\] Cleaning Turnover $145.00


Oct 17 \[Cleaner\] Cleaning Turnover $145.00


Oct 27 \[Cleaner\] Cleaning Turnover $145.00


Oct 14 \[Plumber\] Maintenance Replace water heater valve (receipt attached) $612.40


Oct 31 \[Utility\] Utilities Electric and internet $265.00


Total $1,312.40


Every total in the detail tables matches a line in the summary: rent plus cleaning fees is the gross revenue, the channel fee column is the channel fee line, and the expense total is the expense line. The fee is 20% of $6,620 rent minus $566.10 channel fees. If a number in the summary can't be traced to a row, an owner will ask about it.


## Mistakes that cause owner questions


- **A fee base nobody wrote down.** "20%" of what? Put the base in the management agreement and on every statement.
- **Expenses without receipts.** Agree on a threshold (for example $250) above which a receipt is always attached.
- **Month-end stays split differently each month.** Choose one rule and print it on the statement.
- **Payouts on a different day each month.** Owners plan around that date.
- **Statements that only exist as a PDF in an email.** Give owners somewhere to look up past statements themselves.

## FAQ


### What is an owner statement?


A monthly report a property manager sends a property owner showing rental revenue, expenses, the management fee and the net payout for the period.


### What should an owner statement include?


A header with both parties and the period, a summary that adds up to the payout, every reservation, every expense, the management fee calculation, the payout amount and date, and optionally a few lines of notes.


### How often should I send owner statements?


Monthly is standard, on the same day each month, a few days after month end so late charges and fees can settle.


### Should I attach receipts to owner statements?


Attach receipts for any expense above a threshold you agree with the owner in writing, and for any repair or replacement.


### How do I show a stay that crosses month end?


Choose one rule (by check-in date, by check-out date, or nights in the month) and use it on every statement. Print the rule on the statement so the owner can follow it.


## The takeaway


Put the payout at the top, make every number traceable to a row, write down how the fee is calculated, and send it on the same day every month.
